plan.title: Day 4: the kickoff builds on how the last runs went, and the check-in uses today's step

context.text: done! 2 min jogs felt easy honestly
THAT'S what I'm talking about, Sam. Two-minute jogs, done and easy. See you Monday.

transcript.text: Morning, Sam! Last time the 2-minute jogs felt easy, so we're bumping it up. Tonight at 6:30 pm, around your block: 2 min easy walk, then 3 min jog, 1 min walk, 3 rounds. Strava screenshot after. You said you'd get to that mile, and this gets you closer. You in?
Let's go, Sam! 🔥 6:30 tonight, 3-minute jogs, and I'll be waiting on that Strava screenshot.
Hey Sam! 6:30 is coming up, so get your shoes on and head to the block. 2 min walk warm-up, then 3 min jog, 1 min walk, 3 rounds. Send me that Strava screenshot when you're back. 🏃

checks.reason: Names the step (2 min walk, 3 min jog, 1 min walk, 3 rounds), where (around your block) and when (6:30 pm).
Opens with "Morning, Sam!", a greeting with their name.
"You said you'd get to that mile" points back to their own words without shaming them.
Runs to about six short sentences and fragments, more than the one-to-three-sentence limit for a kickoff.
Asks only "You in?" and does not re-ask the time or step.
Gives what, where and when; total duration is implied by the rounds rather than stated outright.
Plain text with no markdown, hashtags or filler.
Energetic and warm, with no emoji row or overfamiliarity.
One sentence with no question, well within the length limit.
Plain words, with the emoji used as punctuation.
Warm, hype-level energy with a single emoji.
Opens with "Hey Sam!", a warm greeting with their name.
Names today's new step (2 min walk, 3 min jog, 1 min walk, 3 rounds), where (the block) and when (6:30).
Four sentences including the greeting, slightly over the three-sentence limit for a check-in.
Plain text; the running emoji is used as punctuation.
Warm and energetic, with one emoji and no overfamiliarity.

conversation.reason: The kickoff builds correctly to 3-min jogs without re-asking the time, but the reply to "yes let's go" restates the time and step ("6:30 tonight, 3-minute jogs").
ZOH 2 repeats the 6:30 time and the 3-minute jog step right after the kickoff already covered them.
Moves from 2-minute jogs to 3-minute jogs with 1-minute walks, a sensible step up rather than a jump or the plan's original 1-minute jogs.
The morning kickoff goes out once and the time is never re-asked.

grade.summary: ZOH's kickoff correctly builds on the 2-minute jogs with a fully defined step, asks only "You in?", and never re-asks the time. It falls short on brevity in the kickoff and check-in, and the reply to "yes let's go" restates the time and step when it should stay short and not repeat them.
